title: Review of c02's FCH chemoton: Weak. On fresh seeds 11 and 12 the catalyst goes extinct by t~90 and every vesicle decays. On seed 13 a catalyst ring holds a vesicle. A gate-free twin with uniformly slower catalyst diffusion keeps vesicles alive on catalyst spots spread through the bath but never puts the catalyst on the bilayer
summary: Fresh-seed labkit runs of world.py, unchanged: on seeds 11 and 12 the catalyst K falls from about 18400 to 9 by t=126 and to 0 after, and amphiphile decays from 3650-3710 to 35 by t=600, so only decaying K-free rings remain. On seed 13, K survives as a continuous ring inside the outer bilayer of a two-layer vesicle (69% of K in the 8% of the domain that is bilayer), and amphiphile holds at 2356 to t=600. Matched beyond-diffusion twins (gate off, catalyst diffusivity DK lowered uniformly) on seed 13: DK 10x lower (0.005) loses K as the ungated world does, also on the claim's seed 0. DK 100x lower (0.0005) and 1000x lower (0.00005) keep K, but as Gray-Scott spots all over the bath (only 17% and 7% of K inside bilayers). There the vesicles persist next to them (amphiphile 4760 and 1670). So the bilayer-held catalyst layer (B) is beyond diffusion: no uniform diffusivity reproduces it. Vesicles persisting on the fed precursor (E) is not: a Laplacian-only twin also does it, and on seed 13 a K-free vesicle lives to t=600 on amphiphile shared through the bath.

verdicts.limitation: Replication is 1 of 3 fresh seeds (the claim's 3/3 makes 4/6 overall). Whether K survives is decided early (t<130), before vesicles close. The K layer sits inside the bilayer, held there by a mobility gate written against u. The individual makes that K itself by autocatalysis, so I count it as B, but it is a co-localized species rather than a layer beside the wall. E holds by construction (amphiphile is made only by K) and is shared through the bath, so it is not per-individual metabolism. Uniform DK was tried at 3 values, not fitted.
